newsitem.title: UK: Indonesian fuel to keep Swedes powered this winter.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian fuel to keep Swedes powered this winter.

text.p: A Swedish power utility has bought nearly 300,000 tonnes of Indonesia low sulphur fuel oil in September in preparation for the approach of winter.
Sydkraft AB says it has now covered nearly all of its requirement for winter stocks and will have little need to buy from the local European market.
The utility bought the fuel because of its very low sulphur content of around 0.2 percent, which is more environmentally sound than European grades which are 0.3 percent or more.
"We can burn 0.3 percent, but we prefer to burn lower than that," said Sydkraft's Rony Dahlberg.
The utility's foray into the Asian market is not unheard of, but is comparatively infrequent.
"We last bought from Asia about 1-1/2 to two years ago," said Dahlberg.

When buying from markets closer to home Sydkraft purchases from a variety of north European outlets as well as from north and east Africa, but the Indonesian deal was not seen to have hurt the European low sulphur cracked cargo market.
"It does not appear to be having any impact," said a trader of Sydkraft's Indonesian purchases.
"The market is fairly tight as it is and it's unlikely that Sydkraft would have been able to have secured 300,000 tonnes so quickly," said a refinery dealer.
Other traders agreed. "The squeeze caused by such a demand would have rocketted prices," said one.

Sydkraft is set to install in November a scrubbing unit which will give it the flexibility to buy higher sulphur content fuel oil. The function of scrubbing units is to clean gases before they are released into the atmosphere.
